summary: Highest-EV prefill move on the board (turn_1 load is 1.01x and Marlin is 64-68%/47% of its shapes; a 750->450 us expert pair is ~1.33x on the turn_1 load, ~+10% headline). Sound swap-AB design, but SEQUENCE IT AFTER moe s3 (job 3bdec0e58d684c17) is harvested and port from s3's commit with its hazard-free A-fragment variant, because the N16/N32 buckets may be passing by luck.
justification: Mechanism holds: at T=753 ~753 local routes / 32 experts = ~24 rows per expert, Marlin pads to moe_block_size 64 on the mma M side (2.7x MMA waste) and streams 905 MB at ~1.3 TB/s vs the 189 us floor; swap-AB puts the 24 tokens on wgmma N and reads each weight once. The moe and prefill expert dims are identical (K=4096, w13 N=8192, w2 N=4096 K=4096, 32 local experts, same NVFP4 layout), so the port is dimensional, not a redesign. Profile supports it: Marlin 768.6/735.9 us at turn_1 (master check c4d14d62), 649.7/709.5 in submit 502f2eab. Weakest link: the only speed evidence is the moe s2 warm-eager figure (515.9 vs 911.3 us at M=128), and that M=128 timing ran with 64/128-bucket chunks that were producing NaN, so N16/N32 have NO clean timing yet; moe s3 is the first run that prints cold-L2 per-bucket N16/N32 times vs Marlin. Second weak link: the moe s3 review raises a register-A WAR hazard (A fragments rewritten while an RS wgmma is in flight); if s3's variant A (wait<0>) or B (double-buffered a[]) is what fixes N64/N128, then N16/N32 correctness in s2 was luck and the port must carry the fix. Register cap: the real cap is 168 under __launch_bounds__(384,1) (setmaxnreg.inc 232 does not lift ptxas's compile budget); at N16/N32 the accumulators are 8/16 regs so the cap does not bind, and an N16/N32-only instantiation (no 64/128 code in the same function) should drop regs and the w2 8 B spill.
confounders: stack-tonight-five-prefill: supplies the incumbent this gate is measured against (_align_parallel local-routes align + _silu_mul_sorted + Marlin pair); the gate must time new pair vs exactly that, which the hypothesis does. Not a confound of the result, but the new path must consume _align_parallel's Marlin-format (sorted_ids, block_experts, n_padded) at bsm=32, not moe_align_block_size's, and its self-check must run on that output.

experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn: defines MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS=4096; the new T<=1024 branch sits inside _experts_marlin under that gate. Tests with T=300/753 (and the T=200 outliers test) take the new path, so correctness is exercised by the judge's tests too.
interference: No companion. It is a kind:rewrite judged on its own Marlin-replacement rows at turn_1, and its hard prepare gate prints both times and PATH CHOSEN, so a loss means 'gated off' (master re-measured) and a gain is attributable from the kernel rows. turn_1 shape rows drift -7 to -10% on untouched code, so the builder/harvester must read the per-kernel rows and PATH CHOSEN, never the shape z.
rules_flags: Weight repack must stay lossless NVFP4 (permutation of E2M1 codes and e4m3 scales) - stated; assert it in prepare by round-trip.
Branch only on x.shape[0] (shape) and state flags set in prepare; the bucket/chunk table must be built on device (no .item()/.cpu() of counts) so the path stays graph-capturable.
In-process load_inline only; no child process (rules reject process start).
open_questions: Does moe s3 (3bdec0e58d684c17) show the A-fragment hazard is real (variant A/B fixes N64/N128)? If yes, port s3's variant for N16/N32; if s3 fails both variants, still apply variant A (wgmma wait<0> before overwriting A regs) - correct per the PTX ISA, small speed cost.
s3's cold-L2 N16/N32 pair times vs Marlin: if w13+w2 at N32 does not beat Marlin there, the turn_1 port's M1 is unlikely; demote before spending the check.
Grid order: are the chunks of one expert adjacent for the SAME weight N-tile (N-tile major, chunk minor)? Otherwise an expert with >32 routes re-reads its 28 MB of weights from HBM.
Does the soft distribution at T=753 give some experts 100+ local routes (4+ chunks)? Print the chunk histogram in prepare from a soft synthetic routing.
builder_instruction: WAIT for moe s3 harvest; port the _wg_ module from s3's commit (or s2 + wait<0> before any A-fragment overwrite if s3 fails), instantiate a separate N16/N32-only kernel (no 64/128 code in the function) so it compiles under the 168 cap with 0 B local, keep the moe gather/chunker contract but feed it _align_parallel(local_ids, 0, 32, 32) output, order the grid N-tile-major/chunk-minor, and gate on cold-L2 graph A/B at T=753 vs Marlin pair + _silu_mul_sorted at <=0.92x.
